title: Gradient Descent & Optimizers — The Update Is More Than the Gradient
key_insight: Treat the optimizer as a stateful algorithm. Save its moving averages in checkpoints or a resumed run will not truly continue from the same training state.
body:
## The Update Is More Than the Gradient

Two runs use identical gradients but finish differently because weight decay, momentum, clipping, and schedules alter the actual step.

Treat the optimizer as a stateful algorithm. Save its moving averages in checkpoints or a resumed run will not truly continue from the same training state.

Monitor update size relative to weight size. Tiny updates stall learning; huge updates can erase useful structure even when loss has not yet exploded.
common_mistakes: An optimizer creates training labels from nothing.
Weights should move in the direction that raises loss.
Momentum deletes all information from earlier steps.

real_world_usage: Backpropagation finds directions; the optimizer decides the actual size and pattern of every update.
